title: Tokenized throughput accounting and debit/credit protocol for Dedicated
creator: Marta Kim
description: Summary: Define a precise, auditable method for measuring Dedicated throughput with a tokenized accounting model and an explicit debit/credit protocol for customer remediation. Goal: produce contract-friendly SLA language and implementation details engineers and billing teams can use to compute credits automatically. This ticket covers measurement definition, the credit formula, edge cases (multi-region failover, throttled bursts), and required Console/UI hooks for notice and reconciliation.
measurement_spec: Throughput is accounted in 'serve-tokens' where a serve-token equals one model-invocation token processed by the runtime (request+response). Measurement window is the 24-hour UTC rolling window. Primary metric: valid_serve_tokens_per_minute (VSTPM) measured at 1-minute resolution, aggregated to percentiles p50/p95/p99 per customer entitlement. Baseline is the committed tokens-per-minute (CTPM) agreed in contract. Degradation = max(0, CTPM - observed_p95_VSTPM). Error budget burn computed over 30-day rolling window converted to token deficit units. Edge normalization rules: subtract tokens lost due to customer-caused throttles (identified by x-client-drop reason codes) and maintenance windows signaled by scheduled_maintenance flag. All measurements must be reproducible from event logs (log keys: serve.token.count, request.id, model.variant, region).
sla_contract_language: Service Commitment: Redwood will provide Dedicated throughput at the committed tokens-per-minute (CTPM) level specified in the customer agreement. Measurement: Throughput is measured in serve-tokens per minute (as defined in Measurement Spec). Availability shortfall: If observed p95 serve-tokens-per-minute over a rolling 24-hour UTC window is below CTPM, Redwood will calculate a throughput shortfall and apply credit as set forth below. Exclusions: shortfalls due to customer network issues, scheduled maintenance (>=15 minutes pre-notified), and force majeure events will not be counted toward credit. Notice: Redwood will notify customers of incidents that trigger credit calculations within 2 hours and provide a reproducible measurement artifact within 3 business days.
compensation_schedule: Credits are applied as percentage-of-monthly-dedicated-fee based on token-deficit-days within the billing month. Token-deficit-day = sum over 24-hour windows where observed_p95_VSTPM < CTPM of (CTPM - observed_p95_VSTPM) normalized to token-days. Credit tiers: token-deficit-days < 1 => 0% credit; 1-10 => 2% monthly fee credit; 10-100 => 8% monthly fee credit; >100 => 20% monthly fee credit and eligibility for contract review. For partial-month commitments the credit is prorated by active days. Credits are capped at 50% of monthly fee per contract. Credits are automatically calculated and applied to the next invoice unless customer disputes using the dispute process (see Rollout Plan).
examples: Example 1: CTPM=10,000. Observed p95 across window=9,500 for one 24-hour window => deficit 500 tokens/min => token-deficit-day = 500 * 1440 = 720,000 token-minutes normalized per 10,000 => 72 token-deficit-days. This falls into 10-100 tier => 8% credit. Example 2: Burst throttle due to customer-configured rate-limit: excluded when request logs show x-client-drop=rate_limit and client-side rate-limit header present.

open_questions: Should CTPM be enforced at model-variant granularity or pooled across all model variants in the customer's pool?
What is an acceptable minimum pre-notification window for scheduled maintenance to be excluded (15 vs 24 hours)?
How do we instrument multi-region failover so that short-lived cross-region spikes don't inflate deficits?
